questions.question: A shopkeeper marks every item 40% above cost. Cash buyers get a discount of d% on the marked price and card buyers get 2d%. In a month, the cost value of goods bought by card buyers was twice that bought by cash buyers, and his overall profit on cost was 12%. What is d?
questions.solution: Take cost 1 for cash sales and 2 for card sales (total 3). Revenue = 1.4(1 − d/100) + 2 × 1.4(1 − 2d/100) = 1.4(3 − 5d/100). Setting this equal to 3 × 1.12 = 3.36 gives 3 − 5d/100 = 2.4, so d = 12.

questions.question: P, Q and R can each finish a job alone in 20, 30 and 12 days respectively. They charge ₹1,500, ₹1,200 and ₹2,400 per day; a part-day is paid as a full day. Any of them may be hired on any day, and the job must be finished within 8 days. What is the minimum possible total wage bill, in ₹?
questions.solution: Step 1: cost of a whole job by each worker: P 20 × 1500 = 30,000, Q 30 × 1200 = 36,000, R 12 × 2400 = 28,800, so R is cheapest per unit of work, then P, then Q. Step 2: no one may work more than 8 days, so R does at most 8/12 = 2/3. Step 3: the remaining 1/3 is cheapest with P: 1/3 × 20 = 6.67, i.e. 7 paid days. But paying 7 full days wastes part of a day; compare R 8 + P 7 = 19,200 + 10,500 = 29,700 with R 7 + P 8 (7/12 + 8/20 = 0.983, not enough) and with R 8 + P 6 + Q 1 (2/3 + 0.3 + 1/30 = 1, cost 19,200 + 9,000 + 1,200 = 29,400). Step 4: checking all combinations, the minimum is ₹29,400.

questions.question: 12 men can finish a project in 18 days and 18 women can finish it in 24 days. 8 men and 12 women start the project together; after 6 days, 4 more women join them. How many days in all does the project take?
questions.solution: One man does 1/216 of the work per day and one woman 1/432. 8 men + 12 women do 16/432 + 12/432 = 28/432 per day; in 6 days, 168/432. The remaining 264/432 at (16 + 16)/432 = 32/432 per day takes 8.25 days. Total 14.25 days.

questions.question: Solution A is 30% acid and solution B is 75% acid. In what ratio must A and B be mixed to get a 48% acid solution? Enter the ratio A : B as a single number A/B.
A sum of ₹12,000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded half-yearly. What is the interest earned in the first 1.5 years, in ₹?
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7 : 5. After 8 boys leave and 4 girls join, the ratio becomes 1 : 1. How many students were originally in the class?
questions.solution: 7k − 8 = 5k + 4 gives k = 6, so the class had 12k = 72 students.

questions.question: The average of 11 consecutive odd numbers is 47. What is the product of the smallest and the largest of them?
questions.solution: The middle (6th) number is 47; the smallest is 47 − 10 = 37 and the largest 47 + 10 = 57. Product = 2109.

questions.question: For how many integers k with 1 ≤ k ≤ 30 does the equation x² + kx + 36 = 0 have two distinct real roots, both negative?
questions.solution: Both roots negative requires the sum −k < 0 (true for k ≥ 1) and product 36 > 0 (true). Distinct real roots need k² > 144, i.e. k ≥ 13. So k = 13, …, 30: 18 values.

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy |x − 3| + |x + 5| < 14?
questions.solution: For −5 ≤ x ≤ 3 the sum is 8 < 14 (9 integers). For x > 3: 2x + 2 < 14 gives x < 6, i.e. 4, 5. For x < −5: −2x − 2 < 14 gives x > −8, i.e. −7, −6. Total 9 + 2 + 2 = 13.

questions.question: If log 2 = 0.3010 and log 3 = 0.4771, how many digits does 6^20 have?
f is a function on the positive integers with f(1) = 2 and f(n + 1) = f(n) + 2n + 1 for all n ≥ 1. What is f(30)?
How many terms of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, … are needed for the sum to exceed 2000 for the first time?
Real numbers x, y satisfy x + y = 7 and x³ + y³ = 133. What is x² + y²?
questions.solution: x³ + y³ = (x + y)³ − 3xy(x + y): 133 = 343 − 21xy, so xy = 10. Then x² + y² = 49 − 20 = 29.

questions.question: What is the maximum value of 8 − |x − 3| − |2x − 10| over real x?
questions.solution: g(x) = |x − 3| + |2x − 10| is piecewise linear with corners at 3 and 5: g(3) = 4, g(5) = 2. Its minimum is 2 at x = 5, so the maximum of 8 − g is 6.

questions.question: In triangle PQR, the bisector of angle P meets QR at S. PQ = 12, PR = 18 and QR = 20. What is QS?
questions.solution: By the angle bisector theorem, QS/SR = 12/18 = 2/3, so QS = 20 × 2/5 = 8.

questions.question: Two circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm, and their centres are 17 cm apart. What is the length, in cm, of a transverse (internal) common tangent between the points of contact?
questions.solution: Transverse tangent length = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15.

questions.question: A regular hexagon has side 6 cm. What is the area, in cm², of the triangle formed by joining three alternate vertices of the hexagon? Enter your answer as a multiple of √3 (e.g. 27 if the area is 27√3).
questions.solution: Alternate vertices form an equilateral triangle of side 6√3, with area (√3/4) × 108 = 27√3.

questions.question: A right circular cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base at one-third of its height from the apex. The volume of the frustum is what multiple of the volume of the small cone?
questions.solution: The small cone has linear ratio 1/3, so its volume is 1/27 of the full cone. The frustum is 26/27, i.e. 26 times the small cone.

questions.question: What is the sum of all positive divisors of 360 that are odd?
questions.solution: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. Odd divisors are divisors of 45: their sum is (1 + 3 + 9)(1 + 5) = 78.

questions.question: N is the smallest positive integer that leaves remainders 2, 3 and 4 when divided by 3, 4 and 5 respectively, and is also a multiple of 7. What is N?
questions.solution: Remainders are each one less than the divisor, so N + 1 is a multiple of 60: N = 59, 119, 179, … The first multiple of 7 is 119.

questions.question: How many 4-digit numbers have digits in strictly increasing order from left to right?
questions.solution: Choose any 4 distinct digits from 1–9 (0 cannot appear, as it would have to lead); each choice gives exactly one increasing number: C(9, 4) = 126.
